issues.description: Fields 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' have conflicting types between the problem statement UML and the provided implementation. In problem_statement.md the UML declares both attributes as double (lines 65-66). In the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) these two attributes are declared as int (lines 7-8) and related methods (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents()) return int. This inconsistency can confuse students about which primitive type to use for the fields and constructor parameters and whether methods should use int or double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent across the exercise materials. Preferred fix: update the UML and problem text to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (counts are integral) so they match the solution and the int return type of getTotalNumberOfStudents. Also update the template Lecture.java to declare these attributes and the constructor parameters as int. Alternative: if floating-point counts are intended, change the solution fields and any affected method return types/implementations to double consistently.
